chapter: Return to New Orleans and Preservation Hall
title: Starting at the Hall and timeline of Chicago stays
summary: Sayles tries to date when he started at Preservation Hall, corrects himself on coming back from Chicago, and mentions Sweet Emma's band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Why don't you let me ask the question? That's okay. I've already looked into your history a little bit. So you started playing at the Hall, what, probably in the mid-60s?

Well, the Hall had opened up a little bit, but if you had Larry Boyce, he'd open it up for pleasure. And when I came back in 1968 to Chicago, I don't know if that's the exact year. No, no, no, no, no. I'm sure I made a mistake there. It was before that. I had been in Chicago before. But anyhow, I wasn't playing guitar, so I wasn't interested in the music. I played in my younger days. So I used to hang around George Gantt over and go get a profession on my banjo playing, you see? And he used to let me sit in a couple of while, see? And so then they put me with a band. It was a Sweet Dumbas band, Percy. And from there, well, you ask the question from there.
Okay. When did you drop the, well, all right, so you started, when you came back from Chicago in 68, you started at the Hall?
No, no, I came back in 40. That's what I made a mistake of me. Oh. I actually came back in 40.
But didn't you spend a few years, like from 65 to 68, in Chicago again?
I went back the second time. Yeah. For about three years or so.
